newsitem.title: IRAN: Rescue teams search Iran quake rubble for survivors.
newsitem.headline: Rescue teams search Iran quake rubble for survivors.

text.p: Iranian rescue workers on Sunday made last ditch efforts to find survivors as Iran appealed to the United Nations to help victims of a powerful earthquake which killed nearly 2,400 people.

Interior Minister Ali Mohammad Besharati told Tehran radio rescue teams had completed operations in the Birjand area and hoped to be finished soon in Qaen, near the epicentre of the Saturday quake which devastated 200 villages.
He said authorities expected to reach definitive casualty figures after the rescue operations, which they hoped would be concluded on Sunday night.
Rescue teams dug all day through thousands of flattened houses in the remote area in eastern Iran, assisted by grieving relatives who often searched the rubble with their bare hands.

The death toll rose to 2,396 and the number of injured was 6,000, the official news agency IRNA said earlier in a report from Mashhad, capital of quake-stricken Khorasan province bordering Afghanistan and Tajikistan.

The television said initial estimates put the extent of damage in the region at 230 billion rials ($77 million) after the earthquake measuring 7.1 on the Richter scale, Iran's most severe since one in 1990 which killed 35,000 people.
It said 4,300 relief workers set up 9,000 tents for 10,000 families in rural areas outside Birjand and Qaen, known as Iran's saffron capital.
Amid scenes of death and devastation, rescue teams brought out more bodies as children, including toddlers crying, wandered aimlessly amid the rubble.
A make-shift clinic including an operating theatre set up in a sports hall in Qaen was filled with survivors, some on drip feeds. Equipment for three field hospitals was sent to the area.
Iran on Sunday formally asked the United Nations for help in dealing with the disaster which left tens of thousands of people homeless, a U.N. official said.

"The government of Iran has officially approached the U.N. to launch an international appeal for help in coping with the disaster," Iftikhar Ali, head of the U.N. Information Centre in Tehran, told Reuters by telephone.
Iran asked for food, medicine, tents, clothing, water tanks, clothing and four-wheel drive vehicles for relief work in the mountainous area near the Afghan border, he said.
The Saudi-based Organisation of the Islamic Conference, appealed to its 52 member states to extend assistance to Iran.
Several countries including the United States and France said they were ready to help.

Iran's interior ministry earlier appealed for international aid, saying Iran's relief agencies were "ready to receive assistance from those countries that would like to assist the earthquake victims".
Some 130 aftershocks shook Qaen and Birjand in 22 hours after the quake, which hit the area shortly after midday on Saturday, also cutting off power and water supplies, the radio said.
The quake jolted Mashhad, Iran's second largest city with a population of about two million, 370 km (230 miles) northwest of the earthquake's epicentre.
The earthquake toppled a hospital wall in the western Afghan city of Herat, killing five people. A Red Cross official said other casualties in remote areas could not be ruled out. ($1=3,000 rials)
